info.title: UltraV API
info.description:
UltraV is a modern, simple, API-first management layer for KVM/QEMU
virtual machines on single Linux hosts.

**Everything is an API.** Every UI capability is available here first.
This contract is the source of truth for the Web UI, CLI, scripts,
automation, and future AI agents (MCP adapters).

## Conventions
- All requests/responses are JSON.
- Every response includes an `X-Request-Id` header; errors also include `requestId` in the body.
- Errors use a stable envelope: `{"error": {"code", "message", "requestId"}}`.
- Destructive or long-running operations will use specific, semantically
  named operations (never generic `execute`/`command` endpoints).

post.summary: Authenticate and obtain a bearer token
post.description: Validates credentials against the local user database (SQLite) and returns a signed JWT bearer token. All other endpoints (except /health and /ready) require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

put.summary: Change the authenticated user's own password

error.message: A user with this username already exists

delete.description: Requires the `admin` role. The caller cannot delete itself and the last remaining admin cannot be deleted.

409.description: Cannot delete self or the last admin

error.message: Cannot delete the last admin user

get.description: Returns status and identity of the hypervisor host.
Feature discovery for UI, automation and agents. Clients must use this to know what the host supports instead of hardcoding assumptions.
Checks only that the application process is alive. Always returns 200 while the process is up.
Checks that the application and the HypervisorProvider are ready to serve requests.

post.description:
Defines, builds and starts a new directory-based storage pool.
The target directory is created if it does not exist.

409.description: A pool with this name already exists

error.message: A storage pool with this name already exists

delete.summary: Remove a storage pool from the listing
delete.description: Undefines the storage pool (deactivating it first if needed) so it disappears from the listing. No data is deleted: volumes, disk images and files on disk are kept intact.

204.description: Pool removed from the listing (data untouched)

post.description: Re-syncs the pool's volume list and usage numbers with the backing storage.

get.summary: List ISO images in the library
get.description:
ISO images available as installation media. Backed by a dedicated
directory on the host (ULTRAV_ISO_DIR). Files are uploaded via the
browser with `uploadIso`.

post.description: Streams the file into the ISO library. The filename must end in `.iso`.

409.description: An ISO with this filename already exists

delete.description: Removes the file from the ISO library.

post.description:
Creates a virtual network in one of three modes:
- `nat`: routed + NAT subnet managed by libvirt (DHCP + dnsmasq)
- `bridge`: passthrough to an existing host bridge (VMs get IPs on the
  host's LAN; requires a bridge such as br0 configured on the host --
  libvirt cannot create host bridges)
- `isolated`: internal-only subnet, no outside connectivity

400.description: Invalid input (missing bridgeName for bridge mode, bad CIDR, ...)

409.description: A network with this name already exists

get.description:
Host Linux bridges (e.g. br0) that virtual networks in `bridge` mode can
attach to. Creating these bridges is host configuration (netplan /
NetworkManager), not something libvirt or UltraV does; use this list to
detect what exists and guide the user when nothing is available.

put.description:
Updates a virtual network's persistent definition. Fields left null
keep their current value. Structural changes (mode, bridgeName, cidr,
dhcpEnabled) require the network to be inactive (409 otherwise);
`autostart` can be changed at any time. The network name is immutable.

400.description: Invalid input (bad CIDR, missing bridgeName for bridge mode, ...)

409.description: Network is active (stop it before structural changes)

delete.description:
Undefines the virtual network. The network must be inactive
(409 otherwise). VMs keep their interface definitions but lose
connectivity through this network.

409.description: Network is active (stop it before deleting)

post.description:
Stops the virtual network. Running VMs attached to it keep working but
lose new DHCP leases and NAT until the network is started again.

Defines a new virtual machine: allocates a disk volume in the chosen
storage pool and defines the domain (left stopped unless `start` is
true). The VM is not booted from an OS image — attach installation
media with virt-install/virt-manager afterwards if needed.

The `osType` selects a performance profile applied to the generated
domain XML:

- **linux** (default): virtio-scsi disk on an iothread-ed controller
  (`cache='none'`, `io='native'`, `discard='unmap'`), virtio NIC with
  vhost multi-queue, `cpu mode='host-passthrough'` (note: limits live
  migration between hosts with different CPUs — relevant for the
  future multi-host phase), guest agent channel, memballoon disabled,
  catchup timers and a virtio RNG.
- **windows**: everything from the linux profile plus Hyper-V
  enlightenments (relaxed, vapic, spinlocks, vpindex, synic, stimer,
  runtime, frequencies, reset, tlbflush, ipi — only the ones supported
  by the host's QEMU/libvirt are included), `clock offset='localtime'`
  with hypervclock timer. If `virtioDriversIsoId` is set, the VirtIO
  drivers ISO is attached as a second SATA CD-ROM so the Windows
  installer can load `vioscsi`/`NetKVM`. Without it, creation still
  succeeds but `warnings[]` in the response explains the installer
  will not see the virtio-scsi disk.
- **other**: maximum compatibility — SATA disk, e1000e NIC,
  `cpu mode='host-model'`, no enlightenments. Use for exotic guests or
  a first boot of a converted VHDX without virtio drivers.

The NIC model follows the profile (`virtio`, or `e1000e` for `other`)
unless `nicModel` overrides it. A Windows guest on a `virtio` NIC has
no network until NetKVM is installed from the VirtIO drivers ISO; the
response says so in `warnings[]`.

The applied profile is reported back in the returned VM's
`performanceProfile`.

409.description: A virtual machine with this name already exists

patch.description: Changes the VM's hardware configuration: vCPU count, memory size and the attached ISO (install media). Only the fields present in the body are changed (partial update). vCPU and memory changes require the VM to be stopped; the ISO can be swapped in any state and takes effect on the next boot.

delete.description:
Removes a virtual machine. Two levels of deletion are supported via
the deleteDisks query parameter:

* `deleteDisks=false` (default): undefines only the domain
  configuration. The disk volumes remain in the storage pool and can
  be reclaimed or reused manually.
* `deleteDisks=true`: undefines the domain AND deletes its disk
  volumes from the storage pool, freeing the space.

The VM must be stopped (409 otherwise).

parameters.name: deleteDisks
parameters.description: Also delete the VM's disk volumes from the storage pool.

post.description:
Powers on a stopped virtual machine. Returns 409 if already running.

Also 409, with code `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`, when the hypervisor cannot
open a file the domain references (installation ISO, disk volume). The
message names the path. This is a host configuration problem, not a
transient fault: it usually means the backend runs in a container and
the directory is not mounted at an identical path on the host, so the
file is reachable from the API but not from qemu.

get.description:
Upgrades the connection to a WebSocket and proxies binary frames to the
VM's graphical console (VNC/RFB). The browser side is a noVNC client;
binary messages are raw VNC octets. Requires a running VM (409 otherwise).
Note: this endpoint is a WebSocket — OpenAPI cannot fully describe the
upgraded protocol.

101.description: Switching Protocols — WebSocket established, frames are raw VNC

post.summary: Gracefully shut down a virtual machine
post.description: Sends an ACPI shutdown event. The guest OS should shut down cleanly.
Sends an ACPI reboot event. Returns 409 if the VM is not running.

Immediately powers off the VM, equivalent to pulling the power cable.
The guest OS is not given a chance to shut down cleanly; data loss or
filesystem corruption is possible. Prefer `shutdownVirtualMachine`.

VMInvalidState.description: Operation not valid for the current VM state

InternalError.description: Internal server error (no internal details are exposed)

bridgeName.description: Host bridge to attach to (required when mode is bridge).

cidr.description: Subnet for nat/isolated modes (required for those modes).

NetworkUpdate.description: Fields left null keep their current value.

bridgeName.description: Host bridge to attach to (required when mode is bridge).

cidr.description: Subnet for nat/isolated modes (required for those modes).

type.description: Only directory pools are supported for now

targetPath.description: Absolute host path; created if missing

VMState.description:
- running: powered on and operational
- stopped: powered off
- shutting-down: graceful shutdown in progress
- starting: power-on in progress

isoId.description: Optional ISO from the library to attach as install media (CD-ROM, first boot device).

osType.description:
Guest operating system family, selects the performance profile
applied to the domain XML (see endpoint description).

virtioDriversIsoId.description:
Optional VirtIO drivers ISO from the library (e.g.
`virtio-win-0.1.266.iso`), attached as a second SATA CD-ROM for
Windows installations. Only meaningful when `osType` is `windows`;
ignored otherwise. Without it the Windows installer cannot see the
virtio-scsi disk unless drivers are loaded from another source.

nicModel.description:
Network adapter model. Omitted, it follows the `osType` profile:
`virtio` for linux/windows, `e1000e` for other.

`virtio` is the fastest but needs a driver in the guest. Linux has
it in-tree; **Windows does not** — the NIC stays unusable (device
error 43 or an unknown Ethernet controller) until NetKVM is
installed from the VirtIO drivers ISO. Pick `e1000e` for a Windows
guest that must have network on first boot, or `rtl8139` for very
old guests without an e1000e driver.

VirtualMachineUpdate.description: Partial update of a VM's settings. Only provided fields are changed. vCPU and memory require the VM to be stopped. For isoId, a filename attaches/swaps the install media and an empty string detaches it.

isoId.description: ISO filename from the library to attach/swap; an empty string detaches the current ISO.

networkId.description:
Moves the VM's network interface to another virtual network.
Requires the VM to be stopped (applied to the persistent config).

usedBytes.description: Space currently allocated for this disk on the host (the backing volume's allocation, not the guest filesystem usage). Null when the hypervisor cannot report it.

VmMetrics.description: Point-in-time resource utilization of a running virtual machine. The whole object is absent while the VM is not running. Individual fields are null when the host cannot report them (e.g. no balloon driver / guest agent, or a first sample with no previous sample to diff against). Values are computed by the hypervisor provider, which is allowed to keep a short-lived sampling cache per VM.

cpuPercent.description: CPU utilization relative to the VM's allocated vCPUs.

memoryUsedBytes.description: Guest memory currently in use. Null unless the guest balloon driver or agent reports it.

networkRxBytesPerSecond.description: Inbound network throughput across all interfaces. Null until a second sample is available to compute a rate.

networkTxBytesPerSecond.description: Outbound network throughput across all interfaces. Null until a second sample is available to compute a rate.

sampledAt.description: When the underlying sample was taken.

isoId.description: Filename of the ISO currently attached as install media (CD-ROM), if any.

osType.description:
Guest OS family detected from the domain XML (presence of Hyper-V
enlightenments implies `windows`; VMs created before profiles
existed may report `null`).

warnings.description:
Non-fatal notices, populated only in the create response (e.g. a
Windows VM created without a VirtIO drivers ISO). Absent/null on
reads.
example: Windows without a VirtIO drivers ISO: the installer will not see the virtio-scsi disk until vioscsi is loaded from another source.

PerformanceProfile.description:
Performance-oriented settings applied to the domain XML at creation,
as detected from the domain (null for VMs created before profiles
existed).

cpuMode.description: `<cpu mode>` applied. host-passthrough gives best performance but limits live migration between hosts with different CPUs (multi-host phase concern).

diskBus.description: Disk bus applied (virtio-scsi for linux/windows profiles, SATA for other).

ioThreads.description: Number of iothreads dedicated to the SCSI controller (0/absent when not applied, e.g. the `other` profile).

nicModel.description: Network adapter model applied (null for VMs created before this was recorded).

hypervEnlightenments.description:
Hyper-V enlightenments actually present in the domain XML (only
for `windows`; only the ones supported by the host's
QEMU/libvirt, as detected from domain capabilities).
